item.title: French regulator fines Novo Nordisk and Lilly for weight loss ads
item.description:
• Summary: French regulators fined Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly for misleading advertising campaigns for weight loss drugs, stating the ads overstated benefits and downplayed risks.
  • MoAs: GLP-1 receptor agonist (semaglutide), GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist (tirzepatide)
  • Sources: STAT News

item.title: Biotech startup model with Chinese assets
item.description:
• Summary: A new biotech startup model is emerging where small teams raise large checks to license and develop Chinese-originated assets. This approach leverages lower initial R&D costs and established preclinical data from Chinese partners to rapidly advance candidates into clinical trials in the US and Europe. The strategy is attracting significant venture capital.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: Endpoints News

item.title: Opinion: Gene therapy evidence problem
item.description:
• Summary: An opinion piece argues that gene therapy faces an evidence problem, as recent FDA decisions highlight insufficient long-term data and durability endpoints. The author calls for more rigorous clinical trial designs and standardized outcome measures to better assess gene therapies' risks and benefits. The article points to examples where accelerated approvals have led to uncertainty.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: BioSpace

item.title: First FDA ODAC meeting without Pazdur
item.description:
• Summary: The first FDA Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting without Dr. Richard Pazdur highlighted conceptual challenges with trial designs and shifting regulatory dynamics.

item.title: Obesity overtakes oncology in pipeline value
item.description:

item.title: FDA action alert for multiple companies
item.description:
• Summary: The FDA issued multiple regulatory actions on a single day, impacting a range of drugs from argenx, AstraZeneca, Daiichi Sankyo, Biogen, Eisai, and Cingulate. Decisions included approvals, label expansions, and post-market requirements, reflecting the breadth of ongoing regulatory oversight in oncology, neurology, and rare diseases.
  • MoAs: N/A (specific drugs not identified from theme)
  • Sources: BioSpace
